title: Pixel Colossus — Vaporwave Scanline Horizon
description: A vaporwave title card anchored by a pixelated Roman bust beneath full-canvas scanlines, palm-tree silhouettes bleeding into a magenta-to-cyan sky, and oversized Japanese halftone display type — distinguished from generic cyberpunk grids by its deliberate cathode-ray, lo-fi television decay.
philosophy: This design exists at the sacred collision of classical antiquity and analog entropy — marble gods rendered in 8-bit dither, Western cultural icons distorted through VHS dropout and cathode-ray scan artifacts until they become something new. It refuses clean vectors, geometric precision, and any gradient that could be mistaken for modernity. It is for artists who understand that vaporwave's ironic reverence is a complete aesthetic worldview, not a Photoshop filter. The speaker is the auteur; the audience arrives already fluent in the reference.
goodFor: Synthwave or vaporwave music release title slides
Japanese-language album or EP launch presentations
Single-hero retro-futurist brand reveals targeting Gen-Z creative audiences
Aesthetic mood-board decks for music video or visual album pitches
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly financial reviews requiring legibility at distance
Academic or clinical data presentations demanding WCAG AA contrast compliance
Multi-slide decks with sustained body copy or bullet lists
Corporate pitches where scanline artifacts read as production error rather than intent
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like a VHS tape of classical antiquity being played on a dying television — marble gods dissolving into 8-bit dither, every surface humming with cathode-ray scan decay. Compositional drama comes from the collision of monumental scale and analog entropy: the bust looms beneath an atmospheric sky gradient while oversized halftone Japanese type crowds the upper register with ironic, reverent weight. The mood is lo-fi maximalism — dense with layered artifacts yet never busy in a modern grid sense. Avoid any smooth, clean, or crisp edge; signal dropout and pixel chunking are the intended finish.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed edge-to-edge canvas with zero outer margin — the entire slide is a controlled signal artifact. The pixelated Roman bust anchors the lower-center third, cropped below the chin and bleeding past the bottom edge as a monumental hero element. Oversized Japanese halftone display title type dominates the upper half in a center-weighted stack, with a subtitle line sitting below it separated by a thin horizontal rule that mimics a cathode-ray scan band. Palm silhouettes flank the lower-left and lower-right corners as compositional wings, and the full-canvas scanline texture runs as a top-layer overlay across every element.

examples.promptCore: A decayed cathode-ray transmission frozen mid-broadcast — the content zone hums with analog warmth, scanline ridges pressing through every surface like static held in amber. Composition is off-balance: a heavy typographic anchor drags left while pixelated imagery dissolves into halftone noise at the opposing edge. Mood is ironic reverence — information filtered through VHS dropout and lo-fi television decay. Avoid crisp vectors; every edge carries the ghost of analog entropy.
